Use one flat list, not separate lists or folders. Each entry: title, status (want / reading / done), and a one-line note (why you picked it, or a date-stamped thought). Keep it ordered by what you want to read next. Why this wins: a personal list is small enough that a single ordered list with a status tag is easier to scan, reorder, and keep current than multiple containers, and a book lives in exactly one state at a time, so it never appears in two places. The 'why I picked it' note lets future-you drop a book without guilt. When to change: if the list grows past ~50 books or you want to group by genre/shelf, add a tag column to the same list (or move to a simple spreadsheet/app with the same fields) rather than creating new lists. Completion check: you can answer 'what am I reading next?' in one glance, and moving a book between states is a field change, not a file move.
